definitions.definition: ut(x,t)=u_t(x,t)=d/dr u(x,r)|_{r=t}, the time partial derivative. Derivative notation uses the usual total derivative convention (zero if a derivative does not exist); no regularity property is granted by this definition.
utt(x,t)=u_tt(x,t)=d/dr ut(x,r)|_{r=t}, with the same total derivative convention.

definitions.type: family of maps ℝ^n×(0,∞)→ℝ^m indexed by j∈{1,…,n}
definitions.definition: dxu(j,x,t)=∂_{x_j}u(x,t), the partial derivative in the jth standard coordinate, with the total derivative convention. Further expressions ∂_{x_j}ut and ∂_{x_j}dxu(j,·,t) denote partial derivatives of the displayed functions; the latter is ∂_{x_jx_j}u.
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u(x,t)|²=|ut(x,t)|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|dxu(j,x,t)|². Norms are Euclidean; the sum is exactly the Frobenius square |D_xu|², with no factor 1/2.
et(x,t)=e_t(x,t)=d/dr e(x,r)|_{r=t}, with the total derivative convention. Its derivative and integral properties are proved, not part of the definition.
E(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}e(x,t) dx, with Lebesgue measure, for t>0. This is the finite energy integral; its use is guarded by absolute integrability of every spatial section of e.

inputs.statement: The functions ut,utt,dxu,e,et are smooth on their stated positive-time domains. For every x∈ℝ^n and r>0, et(x,r)=2ut(x,r)·utt(x,r)+2Σ_{j=1}^n dxu(j,x,r)·∂_{x_j}ut(x,r), and ∂_r dxu(j,x,r)=∂_{x_j}ut(x,r) for each 1≤j≤n. For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable. More precisely, for every τ>0, put J=[τ/2,3τ/2]. There exist a compact C⊂ℝ^n and R>0 such that C⊂(-R,R)^n and u(x,r)=q whenever x∉C and r∈J. Put Q=[-R,R]^n. Its measure is (2R)^n<∞. On (ℝ^n\C)×int J all positive-order derivatives of u vanish. For every r∈int J, the spatial sections of e,et, ut·utt, dxu(j,·,r)·∂_{x_j}ut, ut·∂_{x_j}dxu(j,·,r), and ∂_{x_j}(ut·dxu(j,·,r)), for each 1≤j≤n, are continuous, bounded on Q, zero outside C, and absolutely Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n.

inputs.statement: Let A be a measurable space with measure μ, and V a normed additive commutative group and normed space over ℝ. Let I be an index type, l a countably generated filter on I, F:I→A→V, f:A→V and b:A→ℝ. If eventually in l, F(i,·) is μ-almost everywhere strongly measurable; eventually in l, |F(i,a)|≤b(a) for μ-almost every a; b is μ-integrable; and for μ-almost every a, F(i,a) tends along l to f(a), then ∫_A F(i,a) dμ tends along l to ∫_A f(a) dμ. output.statement: For every t>0 the finite energy integral E is differentiable at t, and E'(t)=∫_{ℝ^n}et(x,t) dx.

locals.declaration: Choose the compact C in N002 for τ=t0.
Choose R jointly with C from N002, so C⊂(-R,R)^n and the support property holds on J.
Choose B≥0 bounding |et| on Q×[t0−η,t0+η], using F001.
Define Vh(h,x)=(e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0))/h if h≠0 and t0+h>0, and Vh(h,x)=0 otherwise.

argument.text: Fix t0>0, put J=[t0/2,3t0/2], and choose C,R jointly from N002. Set Q=[-R,R]^n and η=t0/4. Then [t0−η,t0+η]⊂int J. By N002, et is continuous. The product Q×[t0−η,t0+η] is compact. M010 applied to et on this product gives a finite absolute bound; replacing it by its maximum with zero gives a nonnegative such bound.

produces.statement: There exists B₀≥0 such that |et(x,r)|≤B₀ for all x∈Q and r∈[t0−η,t0+η].

argument.text: Choose B from F001 and define Vh as declared. For every 0<|h|<η and x∈Q apply M006 to the time section of e, on the interval from min(t0,t0+h) to max(t0,t0+h), with derivative et and bound B, evaluating at the upper endpoint. All times in this interval lie in [t0−η,t0+η]. This gives |e(x,t0+h)−e(x,t0)|≤B|h|, also for negative h by symmetry of absolute value. For x∉Q, N002 gives e(x,t0+h)=e(x,t0)=0. Hence throughout ℝ^n, |Vh(h,x)|≤B 1_Q(x). Each valid quotient is a continuous compactly supported spatial function by N002 and is integrable by linearity from integrability of the two density sections. For each x, differentiability of e in time from N002 gives Vh(h,x)→et(x,t0) as h→0 through h≠0.

produces.statement: For every h∈ℝ with 0<|h|<η, Vh(h,·) is continuous, measurable and integrable, and |Vh(h,x)|≤B 1_Q(x) for every x∈ℝ^n. For every x∈ℝ^n, Vh(h,x) tends to et(x,t0) as h→0 through nonzero h.

argument.text: The measurable nonnegative function x↦B 1_Q(x) is integrable: its absolute integral is B|Q|=B(2R)^n<∞, since Q is a measurable box of finite measure by N002. Use M002 with increment filter h→0, h≠0, the real-valued functions Vh(h,·), limit et(·,t0), and this majorant. This punctured real neighborhood filter is countably generated (the punctured intervals of radii 1/k, k positive integer, form a countable base). F002 supplies eventual measurability, the eventual bound, and pointwise, hence almost everywhere, convergence. We obtain lim_{h→0,h≠0}∫ Vh(h,x) dx=∫ et(x,t0) dx.

produces.statement: As h→0 through h≠0, ∫_{ℝ^n}Vh(h,x) dx tends to ∫_{ℝ^n}et(x,t0) dx.

argument.text: For 0<|h|<η, the two density sections are integrable by N002, t0+h>0, and integral linearity gives ∫Vh(h,x) dx=(E(t0+h)−E(t0))/h. Combining this identity with F003 is exactly the difference-quotient definition of differentiability at t0 and gives E'(t0)=∫et(x,t0) dx. The limit is finite because et(·,t0) is integrable by N002. As t0>0 was arbitrary, the differentiability and integral derivative formula hold for every positive time.
